# The step of a sum of one limb, on an array of the program

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `sum_entry_step_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $t$ of $s + x$:

$$t \approx s + x.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sum(x)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 1>>` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds; in the lane order of the build, or, with `kairn::sequential`, in the sequential order (loop `sum_1_entry`) |
| `sum(x, sequential)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `Sequential` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 1>>` |  |
| `sum_fast(x)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 1>>` | for one limb, `sum(x)` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + x$, ties to even.
- $\lvert t - (s + x)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert s + x\rvert$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u$ | $\frac{1}{2^{53} + 1} \approx 1.1102 \times 10^{-16}$ | $\frac{1}{2^{24} + 1} \approx 5.9605 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `sum_entry_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/StepKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/StepKernels.v), against `sum_entry_step_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions sum_entry_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition sum_entry_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s x : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec x ->
  let t := sum_entry_step_1 emin prec tie_even s x in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + x) /\
  Rabs (t - (s + x)) <= (1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1 * Rabs (s + x).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `sum_entry_step_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_1_1 on a guarded element (rule R3). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/sum_entry_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/sum_entry_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of the sum of an array of one limb that the program supplies (milestone2.md, "Folds",
# "Arrays that the program fills"; question 19, decided (a)): the element passes through guard,
# rule R3, then add_1_1. A compiler that inlines the loop into a program that stored products into
# the array cannot fuse them into the addition. Its claims are those of add_1_1.

g = guard(x)
t = add(s, g)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
